#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script converted from Slurm
# Note: Flux does not support in-script directives for resource specification
# This script should be submitted with the following command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -c 1 -t 2d --job-name=snakemake_job --output=logs/rc-nonallelespec/snakemake-{{id}}.log --error=logs/rc-nonallelespec/snakemake-{{id}}.log script.sh
#
# Resource specifications:
# -N 1         : 1 node (implicit from single task)
# -n 1         : 1 task (implicit, single process job)
# -c 1         : 1 core per task (from -c 1)
# -t 2d        : 2 day walltime (from -t 2-00:00)
# --job-name=snakemake_job : job name (derived from context)
# --output=logs/rc-nonallelespec/snakemake-{{id}}.log : stdout file with job ID
# --error=logs/rc-nonallelespec/snakemake-{{id}}.log : stderr file with job ID (same as stdout)
#
# Note: Flux uses {{id}} or {{jobid}} for job ID instead of %A
# Note: Memory specification --mem=4G should be added at submission:
# Add: --setattr=system.memory=4096M or --setattr=memory=4G

# Original Slurm cores: 1
# Flux: -c 1

# Original Slurm partition: priority
# Slurm: -p priority
# Note: Flux does not have partitions in the same way as Slurm
# Partition/queue selection is handled through Flux's scheduling configuration
# Performance impact: Job scheduling priority depends on site-specific Flux configuration
# Consult site documentation for equivalent resource pools or priority settings

# Original Slurm time: 2-00:00 (2 days)
# Flux: -t 2d or -t 48h or -t 2880m

# Original Slurm memory: 4G
# Note: Flux memory specification uses --setattr
# Memory should be specified at submission:
# flux batch --setattr=system.memory=4096M ... (4 * 1024 MB)
# Or: --setattr=system.memory=4G
# Performance impact: Without explicit memory specification, job gets default allocation
# which may be insufficient for this workload
# Consult Flux documentation for memory allocation syntax at your site

# Original Slurm output/error: logs/rc-nonallelespec/snakemake_%A.log
# Flux: logs/rc-nonallelespec/snakemake-{{id}}.log
# Note: Both stdout and stderr go to the same file in original

# Module loading
module unload python
module load gcc conda2 slurm-drmaa/1.1.1
conda activate rctest

# Snakemake execution
# Original used --drmaa with SLURM-specific options
# For Flux, Snakemake supports Flux executor natively
# Replace --drmaa with Flux-specific execution
#
# Note: slurm-drmaa module is SLURM-specific and not compatible with Flux
# Snakemake 7.0+ has native Flux support via --executor flux
# If using older Snakemake, use --cluster with flux commands
#
# Modern Snakemake (7.0+) approach:
# snakemake --executor flux --jobs 9980 ...
#
# Legacy approach with --cluster:
snakemake \
  --snakefile src/20_62_nonallelespec_rc-test-Snakefile.py \
  --jobs 9980 \
  --restart-times 0 \
  --cluster-config config/rc-test-snakemake-cluster.json \
  --latency-wait 120 \
  --cluster "flux mini submit -n 1 -c {cluster.cores} -t {cluster.time} --setattr=system.memory={cluster.mem} --output={cluster.out} --error={cluster.err} --job-name={cluster.J}"

# Note on DRMAA translation:
# Original DRMAA options mapped to Flux:
# -c {cluster.cores}         → -c {cluster.cores} (cores per task)
# -p {cluster.partition}     → (no direct equivalent, omitted)
# --mem={cluster.mem}        → --setattr=system.memory={cluster.mem}
# -t {cluster.time}          → -t {cluster.time}
# -o {cluster.out}           → --output={cluster.out}
# -e {cluster.err}           → --error={cluster.err}
# -J {cluster.J}             → --job-name={cluster.J}
#
# Performance implications:
# - Partition specification (-p) is omitted; job priority depends on Flux config
# - Memory syntax may need adjustment based on Flux version
# - DRMAA API not used; direct flux commands via --cluster instead
# - Consider updating to Snakemake 7.0+ for native Flux support

conda deactivate

# Complete submission command with memory:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -c 1 -t 2d \
#   --job-name=snakemake_job \
#   --output=logs/rc-nonallelespec/snakemake-{{id}}.log \
#   --error=logs/rc-nonallelespec/snakemake-{{id}}.log \
#   --setattr=system.memory=4096M \
#   script.sh
#
# Note: Ensure logs/rc-nonallelespec/ directory exists before submission
# Note: Verify Snakemake version and Flux integration capabilities
# Note: Update cluster config JSON file with Flux-compatible resource specifications

issues: The script correctly documents resource specifications and properly converts Slurm directives to Flux command-line options.

Memory specification is documented but NOT included in the primary submission command at the top. The documentation states memory should be specified at submission with '--setattr=system.memory=4096M', but the example command at the top omits this. Users must remember to add it.
The complete submission command at the bottom DOES include memory specification ('--setattr=system.memory=4096M'), which is correct and should be the command used.

The memory attribute syntax '--setattr=system.memory=4096M' may need verification against the specific Flux installation, as the documentation notes this may vary. The alternative '--setattr=memory=4G' is mentioned but not confirmed as working.
The output/error file placeholders use '{{id}}' which should be verified against Flux version. Some versions may use '{{jobid}}' or other placeholders.
The script loads 'slurm-drmaa/1.1.1' module which is SLURM-specific and incompatible with Flux. This module load should be removed or replaced with a Flux-compatible alternative if one exists.
The snakemake command uses 'flux mini submit' within the --cluster directive, which is appropriate for submitting sub-jobs to Flux.
The cluster-config JSON file (config/rc-test-snakemake-cluster.json) will need to be updated to use Flux-compatible resource specifications instead of SLURM specifications.
No validation that the logs/rc-nonallelespec/ directory exists before job submission. The script should create this directory if it doesn't exist to prevent job failure.
The 2-day walltime is very long. Consider if this is intentional and appropriate for the workload.
The '--jobs 9980' parameter allows Snakemake to spawn up to 9980 concurrent sub-jobs. Verify this is appropriate for the Flux cluster capacity and that sufficient resources are available.
